subject.title: [Security] Session hijacking vulnerability due to predictable sequence IDs in gateway client

question: Should this report be closed as an unsupported sequence-number attack, or retained temporarily for a private exploit reproduction?
rationale: Source inspection contradicts the proposed mechanism, but protected security handling reserves final vulnerability disposition for a human owner who can evaluate any private evidence.

options.title: Close unsupported claim
options.body: Close after confirming that event sequence numbers are ordering metadata and that no client-controlled sequence value bypasses authenticated RPC dispatch.

options.title: Request private proof
options.body: Keep the report open briefly and require a concrete private reproduction showing unauthorized connection adoption, RPC dispatch, or message injection.

recommendation.title: Close unsupported claim
recommendation.body: Close after confirming that event sequence numbers are ordering metadata and that no client-controlled sequence value bypasses authenticated RPC dispatch.

likelyOwner.reason: The gateway transport and connection boundary trace most directly to this person's feature history.
